body:
Marlin Equity Partners has taken a minority stake in Rystad Energy, transitioning Lars Erik Nicolaisen to CEO and Jarand Rystad to executive chairman

Rystad Energy has agreed to sell a minority stake to technology-focused private equity firm Marlin Equity Partners and will change leadership, with founder Jarand Rystad stepping aside as CEO. Deputy chief executive Lars Erik Nicolaisen will succeed Mr Rystad starting 12 October 2026.

Marlin’s investment will support Rystad Energy’s expansion across data, analytics, advisory services and AI technology. This includes Spektra, a technology ecosystem launched in August that combines web-based workspaces, Model Context Protocol connectors and an API gateway.

“Energy markets are becoming more complex, and decision-makers increasingly rely on granular, independent analysis to navigate them,” said Mr Rystad.

Mr Rystad, who has led the company since 2004, will retain a controlling interest and become executive chairman. Mr Nicolaisen has served as deputy CEO for the past eight years.

Mr Nicolaisen said the company would continue investing in its energy experts and in delivering data and insight through its platform, APIs and MCP connections.

Marlin, which specialises in software, technology and services, has nearly $10Bn in capital commitments and has completed more than 270 acquisitions since its founding in 2005.
